Misao Okawa, who was the oldest living person in the world, has died. She was 117 years old. Okawa died on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan. Tadahi Uchimura, a city official, told CNN about her death. She leaves three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family owned a shop that sold kimono (traditional Japanese clothing) in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, who works at the nursing home where Okawa has lived since 1997, told CNN. "She was a kind person, and loved to eat a lot. Her favorite food was sushi and udon noodles," Yoshioka said. "She ate a lot of cake

Documents show that the Missouri National Guard used military terms like "enemy forces" and "advers" to describe protesters when they prepared to go to Ferguson, Missouri, last year to help stop the protests. The National Guard went to Ferguson to support police officers. Many community leaders and civil rights activists said the police used too much force and made the already tense situation worse during the protests, which happened sporally from August until the end of the year.

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) — Gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in the capital on Tuesday. The attack started with a suicide car bomb. It killed at least 12 people and hurt 16 others, officials said. The Islamist militant group Al-Shabaab took responsibility for the attack in central Mogadishu, its spokesman Abu Musab said. The attack began when two suicide bombers blew up their car at the entrance of the two-story building. The building is the home of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Higher Education, Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said. Five gunmen then entered the building and shot people inside, Yusuf said.

One war was enough for 87-year-old Gregory Margolin. When he was 16, he was a Jewish soldier in the Soviet Red Army. He fought the Nazis during World War II while his family fled to safety. Margolin says, “I did not show that I was Jewish,” but it did not matter because people were being killed left and right. All around me.” This year, in Ukraine, he found himself again surrounded by war. Margolin was a sniper who rose to be a commander in the army. His old uniform is still adorned with medals from his time in the military. His granddaughter Liora still marvels at his stories from the war. She is amazed that he managed to survive.

It is exactly 365 days since more than 200 Nigerian school girls were taken from their boarding school in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They are still missing. The Nigerian government and the rest of the world have allowed this to happen. We should all feel ashamed. It is shameful that fan criminals can harm young girls without facing punishment. It is also shameful that people quickly forget about such terrible events.

Norway is becoming the first country in the world to stop using FM radio. by switching to digital radio. The change will happen in two years. People will still be able to listen to radio, but they will use digital technology instead.

Many Nor people have already made the switch. There are only five stations on FM radio, but there are four times as many on digital radio. Half of the country already listens to radio digitally, according to the Culture Minister.

Everyone is big fan of a good comeback story, especially when it involves dinosaurs. A new study suggests that the Brosaurus should have its own name again. For more than a century, science books did not recognize the Brontosaurus as a separate type of dinosaur. O.C. Marsh first named the Brontosaurus in 1879. He did this after receiving 5 crates of bones found at Como Bluff in Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. The dinosaur was similar to, but not as large as the Apatosaurus discovered a few years before. Marsh named the dinosaur, "Brontosaurus," or "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda has offered a reward of 20 kilograms of gold (about $774,000) for anyone who kills or captures two men: Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. The group, called Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), made this offer in a online news release and a wanted poster. They called these two men “the two heads of evil.” AQAP is one of many groups fighting for control of Yemen.

Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old postal worker from Florida, flew a gyrocopter onto the Capitol lawn on Wednesday. He had written about his plans and his reasons on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. The 6-year-old wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot" that the purpose of the flight was to expose corruption in Washington and, more importantly, to offer solutions to the corruption. "My flight is not a secret," the post says. "Before I took off, I sent an Email to info@barackobama.com. The letter is intended to persuade the guardians of the Capitol that I am not a threat and that shooting me down will be a bigger headache than letting me deliver these letters to Congress."

The bad news for Rio de Janeiro continues ahead of the 2020 Olympics. after many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. With just over a year to go before the city hosts the Games' rowing and canoe competitions, officials with the legislative assembly of Rio de Janeiro Monday launched an investigation into the causes of death both in the lagoon and in other lakes and bays in the state in which this phenomenon has occurred. The group will work in partnership with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the Secretariat of State for the Environment.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But he is just now getting used to life outside prison. For nearly 30 years, he was on death row in Alabama. Now, his murder convictions have been canceled, and he walked out of a county jail in Birmingham last week. He told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin that he still feels like he is dreaming. He said, “I have to pinch myself to tell myself that I'm free. It's going to take a little time, but I'll get used to it.”. For 30 years, he spent most of his time locked in a 5-by-7 cell.

The results of opinion polls after the UK election debate were a very close call. The debate had seven party leaders: David Cameron ( Conservatives), Ed Miliband ( Labour), Nick Cegg ( Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage ( UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett ( Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon ( Scottish National Party), and Leanne Wood ( Plaid Cymru, the Welsh Nationalists). There was no clear winner. Comres for ITV, who organized the debate, said Cameron, Miliband, and Farage were tied for first place with 21% and Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. ICM for The Guardian said Miliband was 25, Cameron was 24, Farage was 19, and Sturgeon was 17.

Facebook might soon have a new relationship status: "Just got served divorce papers." A judge in New York has ruled that using Facebook is a legal way for a woman in Brooklyn to give her husband divorce papers. Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband for many years, says her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell. But, Spinnell said, he and his client haven't been able to find Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku to serve him the papers. Baidoo has been able to reach her husband by phone and "he has told her that he has no fixed address and no place of employment," according to court documents.

A person has a terrible accident, and they are in the hospital, brain dead, and on life support. Doctors ask the family to donate organs to save up to eight people. Instead, the family is asked to give the whole body to save just one person. This person might be a quadripleg, with a strong mind but a broken body. This sounds like a science fiction movie. But, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are close to doing this. He calls the project HEAVEN. HEAVEN stands for head anastomance venture. anastomance means surgically connecting two parts.

Police say that Anthony Stokes’s story ended in tragedy on Tuesday. The 13-year-old, who had received a heart transplant, died after his car crashed into a pole. This happened after he was involved in a series of crimes: he stole a car, broke into a house, shot at an elderly woman, and led police on a fast chase. In 231, Stokes’ family told reporters that an hospital in Atlanta had refused to give him a new heart because he had not followed the doctors’ instructions. Mark Bell, who spoke for the family, shared this information.

It was before sunrise at Garissa University College in Kenya. most students were sleeping. A few had already gotten up to go to early morning Christian prayers. Then the attack began.

 Around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday, attackers made an explosion and started shooting at the front gates of the school. They kept shooting as they walked through the campus. The Red Cross said they went to a girls' dormitory. At one time, they broke into a room where Christians were gathered and took people hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, 25, died in police custody 15 days ago after he was arrested on a weapons charge. His death from a severe spinal cord injury sparked widespread outrage toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray's death in custody is the latest in a string of high profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many have demanded answers about what happened to Gray and his funeral drew civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody.

I have been working as a chef since I was 14. I became a food activist much later, in 2007. That year, my wife was mentoring a young girl who was searching through trash for food to eat. This made me start Food Policy Action. I became active in politics about many food issues, like hunger and factory farms. I have not been alone in this work. One of the biggest catalysts has been "The Meatrix," a 2003 animation parody based on "The Matrix" and produced by the GRACE Communications Foundation, which crystallized the public health risks and environmental harms of factory farming

Dan Swangard is a doctor. He has seen many patients dying in hospitals. He has seen them connected to pain medicine and feeling very scared. He has watched people suffer for weeks or months while their families stood by, feeling helpless.

Now, this topic is personal for him. In 2213, he was told he had a rare, serious cancer that had spread to other parts of his body. Surge doctors removed parts of his pancre, liver, and all of his spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked well. But Swangard, who is 48 years, knows the cancer might come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against Houthi rebels and their allies in the city of Aden. The special forces were in Yemen for non-combat jobs, such as “coordinating and guiding” the battle against Houthi forces and fighters who support former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They also helped drop weapons and communication equipment by parachute. Meanwhile, the source said that Houthi rebels left the presidential palace and other important places in the southern port city of Aden after strong Saudi air attacks. The withdrawal was a change from rebel gains the day before, when Houthi forces took the presidential palace.

Mitchelle Angela Blair, a mother from Detroit, was arrested last month and charged this week with murder and torture. This happened after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer.

On Wednesday, Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy officially charged Blair against killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

According to Detroit Police Chief James Craig, the bodies were wrapped in plastic inside the freezer. They were found on March 24 by a bailiff who was carrying out a court ordered eviction.

 The Wayne County medical examiner has now determined that Stoni died from multiple blunt trauma injuries and Stephen from multiple blunt trauma and thermal injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the world heavyweight boxing champion, has a important title fight coming up. But he is still thinking about the fight for democracy in Ukraine. He talked to CNN from his training base in Miami. The fight is on April 25 in New York against American challenger Bryant Jennings. Klitschko said the crisis in his home country makes him shocked and upset. He said, "My country is unfortunately suffering in the war with Russia. It is not that Ukraine tried to give any aggression to any other nation, in this particular case Russia, unfortunately it's the other way around."

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" this weekend, for the third time. He made a small joke about his roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman." Keaton said in his opening speech that many things have changed since he first hosted the show in 1982. "I had a baby — he is 31. I also have a new girlfriend — she is 28," he said. Some fans were hoping to see Keaton act like his famous characters. They might have been a little disappointed. SNL actors Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a song to ask Keaton to play Batman and Beetlejuice with them. He only gave them a a couple of short jokes.

A month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. On Wednesday morning, he escaped from an Illinois jail. According to Kankakee County Sheriff Timothy Bukowski, Taylor waited outside his cell, then attacked a guard who was doing his rounds. Taylor beat the guard, took his uniform and keys, and walked out of the jail. He got into the guard’s 2012 brown Chevrolet Equuneux SUV. The 23-year-old, who was was scheduled to be sentenced in May, is nobody knows where he is now. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m.

A New York City detective is suspended for allegedly stealing $300 during a raid on illegal cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis confirmed the news. Surveillance video from News 12 Brooklyn shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. He first thought one of his employees had taken it. When he checked the security cameras, he was shocked by what he saw, he told News 12 Brooklyn.

The Hatton Garden heist, as it will surely come to be known, was every safe deposit box holder's nightmare, every movie director's dream. Thieves using heavy cutting equipment and rappelling gear broke into the vault of an esteemed 60-year-old safe deposit company in the heart of London over the past holiday weekend, possibly taking advantage of as many as four days to rifle through an uncounted number of safe deposit boxes. And they reportedly got away with hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of gems and cash -- even, in the educated guess of one former police official, as much as 200 million pounds, or $300 million

On April 27, South Africa marks the anniversary of the first post-apartheid elections in 1994. The country is now facing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. People are expressing their anger on social media using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica, showing that everyone must stand together against this violence. These repeated attacks against migrants and their property show that South Africa’s dream of a “rainbow nation” is failing. The dream was not just about having people of many ethnic groups living together, but also about everyone— regardless of race or class— living with dignity.

In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, admitted that accepting a ceasefire to stop the eight-year war with Iraq was “like drinking poison.”. The conflict had become a defining feature of the Islamic Republic, which Khomeini had established just one year before Iraq invaded Iran. Khomeini rallied the people, including both supporters and increasing critics, to fight against the enemy. He prolonged the war for eight years, even though Saddam Hussein was ready to agree to a ceasefire, and thereby secured the stability of the Islamic Republic. When the war ended, the economy was in ruins, and his most committed volunteers were no longer present.

The idea of sustainable development is that unchecked capitalism is too powerful for its own good. Global capitalism is growing very fast, the world economy is now doubling in size every generation. But on a finite Earth, with a billion new people being added every 15 years, this fast growth is now damaging the physical environment and the social systems that make life good and decent. Sustainable development offers a way out of this growing crisis. The reality is that unchecked capitalism is the economics of greed.

The United States has many benefits from being a space power. U.S. access to space helps protect the country’s security, defense, and its economy. To handle current and future conflicts, fight terrorism, and stop growing threats around the world, the U States military relies on space technology. These include intelligence satellites, GPS, and communication satellites. However, as global threats increase and the need for reliable space access grows, the U States has a serious problem: it depends too much on Russian technology to meet its national security needs.

On the day before the one-year anniversary of the kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls in Nigeria by the group Boko Haram, Malala Yousafzai wrote an "open letter" to the girls. "Like you, I was a target of militants who did not want girls to go to school," she writes in the letter. The 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner survived an attack by the Taliban, which had singled her out for blogging from Pakistan about the importance of staying in school. In the letter, she calls on the Nigerian government and the international community to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria recently held an election.

On Tuesday evening, South African soldiers sent to stop deadly attacks against immigrants. They went first to Jeppestown, a neighborhood in Johannesburg where the violence started on Friday. While soldiers kept watch, police searched a hostel in the area. Earlier, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government was sending soldiers to places where police are too busy fighting the attacks. She said this was not because the police were doing a bad job.

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards were killed in fighting with militants near the border with Pakistan. The fighting happened on Monday in Negur, a town in the southeast of Iran. Iranian state-run news agency IRNA reported that three militants were killed by Iranian forces during the clash. IRNA quoted Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province, saying that the militants came from Pakistan into Iran. Iranian officials have reportedly asked Pakistani authorities to catch the surviving attackers.

Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos is now the top island in the world according to TripAdvisor. The site gave its Travelers' Choice award to the island. Providenciales moved up from second place last year. It took the top spot away from Ambergris Caye in Belize. Ambergris Caye had been number one for two years. This year it fell out of the top ten. TripAdvisor said it is hard to know why. The winners change each year based on what travelers say.

The "Star Wars" story continues to grow. On Sunday, at the Star Wars Celebration fan festival in Anaheim, California, the plot for the 2061 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" was revealed. Director Gareth Edwards showed a early preview of the film and shared the story details. The movie is called an "anth film" by Disney, rather than a "spinoff". It stars Felicity Jones. The story happens between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" (which is the first "Star Wars" movie from 1177). A group of rebels goes on a secret mission to steal plans for the Death Star. Jones plays a rebel soldier.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) — There is a Persian saying: “A good year is determined by its spring.” For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers—the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, and China—to continue nuclear talks under a “joint comprehensive plan of action” is a sign that this year’s Norouz (the Persian New Year, which began on March 21) will be very good. Although some hardline critics may try to cause trouble and complain that the preliminary agreement is not what they hoped for, for many people it shows excellent progress and that’s what they want.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) — Breaking news update at 11:45 p.m. ET: Two Black men, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means now three of the six council members are Black.

Previous story, published at 6:52 p.m. ET: The sky was dark and the radio was full of warnings about sudden floods. In the rain, Ferguson opened its voting places at 6 a.m. for city elections that usually have very few people voting. But today was different. This was the first city election since white police Officer Darren Wilson shot and killed unarmed Black teenager Michael Brown last August. Since then, this St.

On Wednesday night, near Hebrew University in Jerusalem, one person was killed and another was injured in an attack that police believe was terrorism. The driver, a 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem, was arrested. According to Israel Police spokesman Micky Rosenfeld, he drove into two people who were waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill neighborhood. Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died in the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver is now being questioned by the General Security Services.

The art collection of the late actress Lauren Bacall has been put for sale. Bacall was a famous Hollywood star. The collection has works by some of the best artists of the 20th century. The art was sold in New York on March 31. It had been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles before the sale. Bacall died in August 21214 at age 89. She became famous in 1944 with her first movie, "To Have And Have Not." That was when she met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 21215 Golden Globes, George Clooney paid tribute to her in his award-winning speech.

In Kiev, Ukraine, people worried about who is killing people who worked for Ukraine’s former President, Viktor Yanukovych. This idea was not new, but it became a big concern this week after two famous people were shot and killed in Kiev. One was a former lawmaker who was close to Yanukovych, and the other was a journalist who supported Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former lawmaker, was shot and killed around 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance of his apartment building.

Chile will soon recognize same-sex civil unions. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday. This puts Chile in the group of several South American countries that allow these unions. Bachelet said, "This is a concrete step in the drive to end the difference between homosexual and heterosexual couples," Bachelet said. The new law will take effect in six months. It will give legal weight to cohabing relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The Chilean government estimates that around 2 million people will be able to benefit from the change.

When you next fly to Florida, look out the window. When you take your children to see the talking mouse or go to South Beach for the sun, choose a window seat. As you fly over the Everglades, think about how this place shows the mistakes of people and the price of fixing them. The area near Miami or Orlando looks like a messy swamp full of dangerous animals: snakes, scorpion, rats, roars, alligators, and mosquitoes. A researcher once caught 365,000 bloodthirsty bugs in a single trap in a single night

In early April, ISIS militants took over the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. They flooded the streets in large numbers, wearing masks. The camp had already been under siege and bombed by Syrian forces for more than two years, so the desperate residents faced a new, even more frightening reality. ISIS had defeated several other militia groups in the area. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS militants killed people in the streets, including three people who were caught and killed in front of others. Now, ISIS controls almost all of the camp.

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors have found that their "Great Firewall" is no longer enough. They have created a new cyber weapon called the "Great Cannon." This tool attacks servers outside China, including ones in the United States. The "Great Cannon" works openly and visibly. The study’s authors say this kind of attack on other countries’ soil will likely anger the rest of the world. They also believe Beijing may have expected this reaction.

investigators investigating the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 have not found any evidence of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz caused the crash. A spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that Lubitz had shown suicidal tendencies at some point before he started his career as a pilot. Lubitz did not leave any writings or conversations where he explained his reasons or admitted to any plans, spokesman Christoph Kumpa said. However, medical records show that Lubitz was suicidal at one time and received psycho therapy. This happened before he ever got his pilot’s license, Kumpa said.

The leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels, Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, said on Sunday that his group will not surrender. A top Saudi military official claimed that weeks of airstrikes have significantly weakened the Houthi group. The Houthis are a Shiite group. They took over the capital city, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power. The Saudi-led coalition has been bombing the Houthi group for more than three weeks. The goal is to push the Houthis back. The Houthi rebels said in a televised address that their fighters will not leave the main cities or the government buildings. The leader said, “Anyone who thinks we will surrender is dreaming.”

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a large truck bomb and exploded outside the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. This attack killed 168 people, including men, women and children, and injured hundreds more. It is still the most deadly act of home terrorism in U.S. history. The media covered the attack heavily, with themes such as "attack on the heartland" and America's "lost innocence." In fact, the bombing took the country by surprise. It wasn't just the scale of the tragedy that drew attention, but the fact that the bombing exposed something new: American citizens targeting their own government with a deadliness hith unseen.

If you were worried about something important, would you take action? Would you make a sign, join a protest, or keep trying even when no one else seemed to care? When Boko Haram fighters kidnapped more than 220 Nigerian girls from their school a year ago, millions of people around the world used social media to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people. People from famous stars to world leaders showed their anger by using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It was one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 22014, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The attention on the campaign faded

Barney Frank, a retired U.S. Congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He told a large, enthusiastic crowd about his 45 years of working in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while serving in office. He also criticized politicians who hide their sexual orientation but vote against gay rights. When a audience member asked him about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about the proposal. but he told the young man not to worry about "crazy people."

Al-Shabaab militants attacked Garissa University College in Kenya on Thursday morning. during morning prayers. The attackers shot people randomly and took some hostages. Kenyan security forces killed the attackers.

 Nearly 150 people died, including students. Dozens more were hurt. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack.

 This attack happened only a few months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The group has been responsible for many attacks in the area. It has also recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa is celebrating the removal of a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonial leader. This follows weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue be removed, saying his history is stained by racism. They used the hashtag #RhodesMustFall to voice their opinions in a campaign that began last month. Four weeks later, the hashtag is now #RhodesHas Fallen. The university said on Wednesday that the heritage authority gave them permission to remove the statue from the campus. "These steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the statue while matters concerning its future are resolved," the university said in a statement.

Syria is a terrible place, things are worse, and more people are dying. According to an opposition group, the number of deaths has doubled in one year. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said 310,00 people have been killed since the civil war started. A year ago, the number was 162,402. The year before that, the United Nations said 70,000 people were dead. The United Nations says more than half of Syrians are so poor they need help to survive. Food rations are being cut because there is not enough money donated.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court looking quiet and shy. But prosecutors say she was not afraid to fight a rival. A police report says she called a woman this summer and threatened her. She told the woman, "Leave my man alone" and "Stop looking for him. I know people who can put a bomb where you live." Because she is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev, prosecutors did not think the threats were a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment. She says she did not do it. Last December, she left court with her lawyer. They did not talk about the case.

A door with a graffiti drawing by the British artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday. A police official in Gaza told CNN about the situation. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, went to a court in Gaza. He said he did not know the door was valuable. He sold it for only 175 U U dollars. The police in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, will keep the door. They will keep it until a court meeting. The court meeting will happen on a day that has not been chosen yet. When Darduna’s home in Gaza was destroyed in the war last summer, he said he had nothing left. He only had a doorway and a door.

The Saudi-led coalition’s attacks against Houthi rebels in Yemen continue. The coalition is gaining control, while many people are fleeing and death numbers rise, including many civilians. Five days after the first air attacks, the coalition has destroyed Houthi air defenses and the defenses of supporters of Yemen’s long-time President Ali Abdullah Saleh. and made all but a few air bases and runways unusable, a Saudi source said. Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all Yemeni ports, allowing only closely watched non-military medical goods to pass its blockade, according to the source.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands, stronglyly criticized his fans for booing Spanish player Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called the fans a "disgrace."

 Spain's coach, Vicente del Bosque, played a new team in Amsterdam. Iniesta started on the bench. He came into the game in the 76 minute. The home fans cheered and booed him.

 Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored goals in the first half. This was a good win for the Netherlands. Hiddink was not happy with how Iniesta was treated.

Scotland will know on May 21 if their September 21, 2015, Euro 2016 qualifying match against Georgia will be played without spectators. UEFA has opened disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation (GFF) after fans twice invaded the field during Sunday's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi. European football's governing body is also set to look at charges that allege home fans were guilty of setting off fireworks while a string of safety breaches, including blocked stairs, locked gates and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, will also be investigated. A fan invades the pitch during Georgia's 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

Football agents were waiting on Wednesday for news about new rules. starting April 1, the rules for becoming a football agent will change. Now, anyone can become an agent if they pay £500 for the first year. The FA will charge £250 for each year after that. Agents who already have licenses do not need to follow these new rules. The FA plans to put a link on their website for agents to sign up, but by 1pm, the link was not yet available. Mel Stein believes the new rules will “create chaos.” These new guidelines came after FIFA stopped controlling agents.
